An episode has three kinds of steps. Demonstration steps show the demonstration video, on a task that has one. Execution steps show the scene while the robot carries out a command. One conversation covers one episode. The first user turn states the task goal. Every user turn is one decision step. It adds the steps recorded since the previous turn. All steps of this episode stay above in the conversation, together with your own earlier answers. Use the whole history. An earlier step can be the only record of something that is no longer visible.

Each block describes the scene at that step.

The position is the center of the object's visible pixels in the 256 x 256 front camera image. y is the row and grows downward. x is the column and grows to the right. The center shifts when part of an object is hidden. Several objects of one kind are listed after one name.
  * An object can carry a state, such as being held in the gripper, lifted off the table or pressed down.
  * The gripper line gives the position of the wrist in the same [y, x], its height above the table and how far the fingers are open. "raised out of the frame" means the gripper is above the camera's view.
An object missing from a block is not visible at that step. It may still be there.

so the robot's right-hand side appears on the LEFT of the image.
